When you went to Kroimire you would -- you would ask Fatmir what you should do, how you should set up operations there. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to answer a question, such a long question, but I'll do my best. Of course this is a false description because it couldn't be that I was in Kroimire in April because in May I left for Kacanik and in end of April and beginning of May I was in Shtime area, where together with Ilaz we went to Kacanik afterwards. I explained that this could not have happened overnight, that this process took several days. If I'm not mistaken it took about -- it was around 10th or 12th of May and until the end of May that I moved from Shtime to Kacanik, Ferizaj, that I did this journey, that I went to Gllobocice and after my several-day stay in Kacanik, I returned here. So this description is a false one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, I don't want you to focus on the date at the moment. You testified already in this courtroom that you brought weapons from Kacanik to Kroimire. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And here in your interview you talk about distributing the weapons and -- and then you say: "I usually in contact with Fatmir, that is I asked where we should set up and what operations we should carry out since we were in Kroimire." And then you say: "I asked Fatmir what we should do." Do you see that where you say that in the interview?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that's what happened when you were in Kroimire, you asked Fatmir what you should do. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could have advised or consulted myself with Fatmir, what to do about Kroimire and with the soldiers in Kroimire especially after the problems I faced in the beginning. The description here in a sense of requesting things from Fatmir, it is simply consulting. I wanted his advice what to do simply because Fatmir had created positions in Klecke and was in a better position, an advanced position, as far as organisation was concerned. The Celiku unit was advanced as far as organisation was concerned and our unit was lagging behind. Therefore, I wanted Fatmir to instruct us what to do in Kroimire. I didn't know Ramiz Qeriqi very well. I didn't know the soldiers in Kroimire very well. That's why I saw a need to discuss these matters with these people and I discussed this matter with Ramiz Qeriqi as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you did this after you arrived in Kroimire. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was end of May/beginning of June. These three or four days or two or three days, I don't remember exactly, that I stayed in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you said that -- you were asked if Fatmir Limaj at that time either contacted you or contacted Luan directly and you said: "Yes, with one -- that is another." And you were asked again, "Fatmir Limaj was in contact with either you or Luan?" And you said: "That's right." So when you were in Kroimire, Fatmir Limaj was in contact with you or with Luan. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I contacted with Fatmir on those days or in end of May or beginning of June. I contacted Fatmir once. I cannot describe the contacts with Luan, but as Luan said, there were contacts. I simply know of my contact with Fatmir Limaj in June, in beginning of June, and as I said here I did have a contact. I'm not denying that I had any contacts with him. I did have contacts with Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And then you're asked if Fatmir Limaj is the person who had direct links in the General Staff and you say: "In fact he was the coordinator of this matter." And he was the coordinator, wasn't he, at that time when you were in Kroimire at the end of May/beginning of June?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained this earlier and I will do it again. I described Fatmir Limaj as coordinator of contacts with General Staff because in June, in the beginning of June, I did attempt to contact members of General Staff because there was a great need, a necessity, for ammunition and weaponry. I will say it again that the coordination of Fatmir Limaj was in a sense of placing contact with the General Staff. I always thought -- although it was difficult to know where the General Staff was positioned, but I always thought that the contact could be made in Drenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you needed ammunition and weaponry at the beginning of June, you tried to make that contact with the General Staff through Fatmir Limaj. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if I contacted the General Staff in June, although I know that in May I did contact the member of General Staff Hashim Thaqi, who I learned later was a member of General Staff. In June I stayed in Kroimire for three or four days, I don't know exactly, and I returned to Kacanik. Therefore, the meeting with Fatmir Limaj could have taken place in these days, although I don't remember of such a meeting but it is possible that there was one. But I don't remember. As for the contact with General Staff in June, it is quite questionable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And then as the interview proceeds, the structure is -- a structure is proposed to you and the question is: "If we can describe the structure: We have a General Staff that is above everything and in the middle there stands Fatmir Limaj as a coordinating point, and then the transmission is carried out. The other point where Fatmir Limaj conveys it is where you and Luan are. Is that correct?" And you say: "It is correct." And then you go on to explain that you were also entrusted with the area of Kacanik. But you agreed with the structure as it was described to you, didn't you? General Staff at the top; in the middle Fatmir Limaj as a coordinating point; and then you and Luan at the point in Kroimire? You said that is correct. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way it's put here I wanted to explain some things, to enlighten some things, which I think were normal for me to do because it seemed to me that this -- there was something wrong with this description, especially when it mentions the month of April when my unit was not even organised then in Shtime or in Lipjan. And such form of description was illogical to me. That's why I thought that it needs to be revised, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, sir, I don't want to focus too much on the date because it's discussing April and May here. The question is: When the structure was put to you that there was a General Staff, then Fatmir Limaj, then you and Luan at the points, when that structure was put to you, your answer is: "It is correct." Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot talk of a structure without pinpointing the period, defining the period. First we have to agree on the period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's agree on the period when you are in Kroimire, whether that was in May or the beginning of June. And that was a period that was being talked about here. At that period when you were in Kroimire, there was this structure that was described to you: The General Staff above everything, Fatmir Limaj as a coordinating point, and you and Luan at Kroimire. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I'm saying what I already said yesterday, that the way the structure is described is after the public appearance of Jakup Krasniqi as the KLA spokesperson --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But, Mr. Buja, Mr. Buja, I'm sorry to interrupt you, but is the -- are you now saying this is the structure that existed after the public appearance of Jakup Krasniqi: General Staff at top, Fatmir Limaj in the coordinating position in the middle, and you and Luan at Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I think I explained it very well --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, if you can just answer my questions. Did this structure ever exist?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this period the coordinator between the General Staff and the units that are described here, in the hierarchic sense of the word didn't exist. I mentioned this several times --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, can you explain why in the interview when this was put to you: General Staff above everything, Fatmir Limaj in the coordinating point, and you and Luan in Kroimire, why did you say: "It is correct"? Can you explain that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. During the interview I thought I might make some mistakes during the description; that's why I demanded to make some corrections --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, if this is a mistake, this description, can you explain to us how you made that mistake?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I made the mistake because I wanted to explain the period covered by this description. I wanted to enlighten many issues: The flow of developments of organisation which did not exist at the time I was questioned about. In April, I didn't have a unit at all --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But, Mr. Buja, now you're saying this structure never existed. So the mistake couldn't have been that you were talking about a different period because you're saying that this structure never existed. Do you have any other explanation for how you could have made this mistake, if it was a mistake?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this structure that is described here may have been described as such after June even though it is rather difficult for me to explain the meaning of the structure as such. Even at that time I wanted to explain these issues, but I thought after revising them I might make the corrections and I went on --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But is it your testimony now that this structure may have existed after June? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the periods are rather short, three, four days. And you could talk of a structure. I'm talking about the time when the spokesperson of the General Staff was in Klecke. It is then that you can describe the structure in these words. But when Jakup Krasniqi instructed me that organisation was underway regarding the subzones and they planned to form a subzone in this area, Lipjan, Stimlje, Ferizaj, Kacanik, it was then that I started to work on an entirely new structure of organisation until I was appointed. Those brief periods of organisation that existed which might be described as some structure, but which were in fact not such, might be mentioned. But the form of the guerrilla unit and the links it had with the General Staff, which we cannot say there was a General Staff [as interpreted], but because of the location of Jakup Krasniqi it was in Klecke. That's why we talk about the links of the units with the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, I'm not sure I understand your answer. Are you saying this structure did exist at some time? Did it ever exist, this structure, or no, that you describe in the interview: General Staff, Fatmir Limaj, you and Luan at Kroimire? Did that structure ever exist, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This form of the structure did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Then do you have any other explanation for why you said it did in this interview?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that at that time I didn't -- of the interview I didn't focus much on this. I wanted to explain something but then just ignored it thinking I could go back to it at a later time after I got the transcripts. I just wanted to have that interview done and then later on see how the structuring of the KLA was done because things may be forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, it was put to you a final time in this passage that this structure you -- there was -- Fatmir Limaj -- it's at the end of the passage, it's at the bottom of page 36 on the English: "Fatmir Limaj receives instructions from the central staff and you and Luan in Kroimire receive instructions from Fatmir Limaj. Is this correct?" And your answer is: "That is correct. I wanted to explain something else but it is correct." So now you have said -- in just this passage you have said at least three times that the structure being described is correct. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even here in the transcripts it is written and I am reading: "You and Luan in Kroimire received instructions from Fatmir." And the question is asked of me whether that is correct. And I said Yes, but wanted to explain something else but it's okay. I didn't say accurate, correct. I say Okay, because I wanted to explain something.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What you wanted to explain was your relationship with Luan. Right? That's what you wanted to talk about?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the nature -- not about the nature of relations with Luan, but the nature of the description of the structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you are asked by me at the end of the interview and the part that we just -- we played already whether there was anything else that you wanted to explain, did you go back and say: That structure that you described, that wasn't correct? Did you do that at the end of the interview? It's at page 104 of the Albanian, page 86 of the English.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's page 104 of the Albanian. You were asked if there was anything else that you wanted to say -- anything else you wanted to explain. Did you say then that the structure that had been -- that you had agreed with several times during the interview was in fact not correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read you, sir, from the transcript what I said then. I think most of the issues have been mentioned even though it is difficult to grasp that period, the form of organisation, developments then. However, I think that some have been clarified, that is my point was that some issues were clarified but not the form of organisation. That was not fully clarified. That's why I demanded to have the transcript to correct that, to correct possible mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You -- and you don't say there, do you, that the structure that you had agreed with again and again in the interview was not correct? You don't say that there, do you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that things not all -- not everything has been clarified. Among the things that have not been clarified is also the structure. Some others were already enlightened. And this is what I had in mind, which I mentioned also here, that is the form of organisation was very difficult to explain. And it's very clear that I have stated some issues have been clarified, implying that there are many others that have not been clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, I want to move on to the subject of who were assigned to the different posts in the area, or units if you prefer to call them that. You knew, didn't you, that at Lapusnik Voglushi, Ymer Alushani, or Qerqiz was in charge of Lapusnik in May, June, and July of 1998? You knew that, right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that Voglushi or Qerqizi -- which me seemed more authoritative, Voglushi -- didn't have all of Lapusnik under his command because there were other units there. But there was a unit that Voglushi led; this is what I thought then because officially, even today, I am not clear who the leader of the unit was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But you knew that it was either Voglushi or Qerqizi. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that Voglushi or Qerqizi was the commander of a unit in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the unit that they commanded -- either one of them commanded, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. one or the other, was the Celiku 3 unit. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may say Celiku 3, but I didn't know for sure whether it was Celiku 3 under their command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, you knew that it was a Celiku unit under their command, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that in Lapusnik there was a unit by the name of Celiku 3, but as to who commanded that unit, this I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, which unit did you think that Voglushi or Qerqiz commanded then?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that they might be unit commanders, one -- of one and the other of another unit. I couldn't figure that out then, whether one of them was the commander of Celiku 3 or one was a commander of a unit and the other of another unit. What I knew was that when I had business to do, I addressed Ymer Alushani, Voglushi, who was one of the commanders of the units there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the -- you've already told us that the Guri 3 unit was on the other side of the Pristina-Peja highway. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have described what I heard, but I didn't know this myself, how they were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But you heard that the Guri 3 unit was on the other side of the Pristina-Peja highway. Right? That's what you told us at the end of the day yesterday.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had heard, but to speak here accurately I would hesitate to speak on the basis of hearsay because they might have been just misrepresentation of events. I had heard about this form of the positions of the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you knew that the Lumi units or unit was in Malisevo. Right? You knew that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Lumi unit in Malisheve? As far as I know there were Lumi units elsewhere in other parts, like Lisi units or other units. I know in the Lapusnik gorge there was a Lumi unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You think that there was a Lumi unit in Lapusnik gorge?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that there was one Lumi unit in the Lapusnik gorge. I cannot specify it, but not very certain. I may say that there was. I can't be very accurate and can't say it in full certainty. There were Lumi units either in Lapusnik gorge, which is quite an extensive area, or in Negrovce, or in some other adjoining villages. I can't give you an exactly location. I've mentioned some units that were located or stationed in the Lapusnik gorge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you say "the Lapusnik gorge," you're talking about an area that is bigger than the village of Lapusnik. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to turn to page 43 of the Albanian transcript, and it's page 40 of the English. And on the Albanian it's -- it's about at the top of the page 43, and on the English it's two-thirds of the way down on page 43 -- on page 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if we could have the -- switch to the Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "S.B.: Well, I can -- well, I used to know them mostly by their nicknames. "O.L.: Yeah, nickname is okay. "S.B.: Voglushi or Qerqiz, one of them was for Lapusnik. Voglushi would come -- would often visit Kroimire. So he would come and bring along backup units to help us during the offensive. The soldiers from Lapusnik were stationed here in Fushtice. So it was a sort of competition who would set up more points among the commanders. It was problematic in a way because you had to move soldiers from one point to another point in order to [inaudible] -- so there was a sort of overlapping responsibilities, interference with each other. So it's not -- this is my responsibility now, these are my soldiers, these are your soldiers. Yeah, I can't remember the name of the person in charge there because of this fact. "O.L.: Okay. "S.B.: There's been -- there's been many changes here -- "O.L.: Okay. "S.B.: -- meaning this point. Kroimire would serve as a gathering point for soldiers. There was no such thing as a stationed unit in that place. I and Luan used to stay here, so I -- Luan stayed here often. Kumanova used to stay in Klecka. "O.L.: Okay. "S.B.: So Kumanova was thought at least at that time by us as the highest-ranking person in Klecka, and Celiku was considered or was thought to be by us some -- higher up than Kumanova. "THE INTERPRETER: Can I ask again who was the highest-ranking person in Klecka? "O.L.: Yes. "S.B.: According to what we thought, Kumanova was the highest-ranking person in Klecka. Later Kumanova moved with units here and was stationed in Luzhnice and also the other point. And on the other side of the asphalt road in Grejcec. So anybody who tried to stand and to -- to expand and increase the number of these points. "O.L.: Okay. Do you want to do a clarification on that? "A.W.: Yeah. The way I understand what you're saying is that Kumanova has responsibility for Klecka but that Celiku is above him in the structure. That's at least what I've understood you to say. Is that right? "S.B.: So we thought Celiku was above -- was above this structure. "A.W.: But he was also in Klecka? "S.B.: Yes, he was in Klecka. Yeah, it was at that time end of July, July 1998, that there happened to be that other members who were thought to be members of the General Staff used to stay in Klecka, or at least we thought that they were from General Staff, from main headquarters. "A.W.: But also during May, June, and July, all during those months Celiku was in Klecka. "S.B.: Yes, yes, he was there. "O.L.: And I'm still trying to clarify a little bit the role of Kumanova now, him being -- you're saying the highest ranking in Klecka. Did that mean that he -- that he was giving orders to these other points or was he just the leader of the soldiers in Klecka? "S.B.: I can't say because my contacts, my meetings, were with Celiku. "O.L.: Okay. "S.B.: But Kumanova would be -- would happen to be present there as well during my meetings with Celiku. So it was more -- it was more work based on consultations rather than orders. So let's say I was -- I was consulted or I was consulting or I was discussing about the weapons supply -- "THE INTERPRETER: I'm sorry was a mistake. "S.B.: Weapons supply, yeah, that's correct. So it was -- there were sort of deliberations, so it's better not to do this or do that. If Celiku was not able to give a definite answer to questions that would arise then, he would turn to the general -- to main headquarters to get clear instructions. "A.C.: Can you just draw in above Klecka the linkage of the main headquarters to the KLA, just to complete the diagram. "S.B.: No, well it's -- yeah, I'll put momentarily as a main headquarters. Also I can't say it was the other thing, but let's leave it that way for a moment. "O.L.: Just to" --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm mindful of the hour and what the Court said earlier about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Two things. The second matter: Given the progress today and given that I understand the occasion will continue beyond 7.00, I think the most we can hope to do is to conclude our hearing a little earlier than 7.00 but otherwise continue on until then. The second -- other issue is whether this is a convenient time or do you want to ask some questions at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I could ask about ten minutes of questions about this passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, did you see in this passage where you said that you considered -- you said: "We considered Celiku that is in fact above our organisation."

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it and I saw other mistakes as well. Kumanova was the commander of Luzhnice unit, not in Klecke.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's right. He was the commander in Luzhnice. But my question is: What did you mean when you said: "We considered Celiku above our organisation"? What did you mean when you said that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I explained earlier. We supposed that he was in a higher position than we -- than us because of his qualities that I mentioned earlier, political expertise and general background. This is why we thought that this man whom we respected was in a higher position, but these were just suppositions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But then later in the passage that we've just looked at you say: "When Celiku was unable to explain to me, that means in fact that he asked for time to consult with members of the General Staff." And that happened, didn't it? You would go to Celiku with something and if he could not answer it he would ask for time to consult with members of the General Staff. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I explained I think very well. It was not the form of orders; it was a form of consultation. We consulted one another about many things related to our organisation. Of course when we failed to find explanation, Fatmir insisted and I insisted that we clarify these issues with the General Staff. But this doesn't mean that there was a hierarchy and that Fatmir Limaj was asked or was supposed to clarify these issues with the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if issues had to be clarified with the General Staff, it was Fatmir Limaj who would do it? He would clarify matters with the General Staff and then get back with you later. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July I too went to the General Staff to meet the spokesperson June/July to clarify things; we could do that. If we were unable to agree on a common view about an issue, we took it up with the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, can -- you said in the interview: "He asked for time to consult with members of the General Staff." Did that ever happen, that he would ask for time to consult with members of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recollect that he has asked for time, but when it came to issues we couldn't resolve we couldn't do that without contacting the General Staff. This might be done through Fatmir or I could do that through contacts with the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But that's not what you said here. You didn't say: One of us would contact the General Staff; you said: "Celiku would contact the General Staff." Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I keep repeating now and again that numerous mistakes occurred during this interview. Normally during this period, end of June/beginning of July, especially in July, was the commander of subzone [as interpreted]. And didn't need anyone's intervention, or in this case Fatmir Limaj's intervention with the General Staff, because as a commander of a subzone, I kept direct links with the General Staff. As of mid-July, I began to know almost all -- most of the members of the General Staff and especially Jakup Krasniqi. In this period, I didn't require Fatmir Limaj to establish contacts for me with the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume just after 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may again, just for the record. Every break gives us opportunity to make further progress, and I've confirmed that the notes were contemporaneous; they were prepared at the time of the meetings. And secondly, the letter has been found and it will be provided to the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I'm wondering if the Court has a sense of when it wishes to stop today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When you finish or a quarter to 7.00, whichever is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You've put me in a spot, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to please turn to page 64 of the Albanian transcript; it's page 55 of the English transcript. And on page -- on the Albanian I draw your attention to the middle of the page and if we could have the clip. And on the English it's at the bottom of page 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think we need to have the Sanction on. We'll start it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "O.L.: Okay. So once again I want to go back to the period of June and July of 1998 and the area that was under the headquarters of Klecke. So was this organisation that you -- that you've drawn to us on this piece of paper, was this effective during this time period that you're calling the first offensive? "S.B.: Yeah, there were points at the time existent. "O.L.: And this was approximately the organisation in -- under the headquarters of Klecka?"

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Buja, in that part of the interview you're asked: "You've already drawn the picture, the diagram," and I believe it's still in front of you. If the usher could assist that it's still in front of the witness U003-3675. I believe it's under the binder there. You've already drawn this diagram during the interview and here, at this part of the interview, you're asked if at the time of the first offensive the organisation that you have described in this drawing is effective, that this was approximately the organisation under the authority or under the command of Klecka. And you say: "That's right." And in fact, that is correct, isn't it, that this diagram that you drew of the units under the authority or command of Klecka, this was how it was at the time of the first offensive, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time of the first offensive, a system that functioned and which you know very well, but I was appointed commander of the subzone, operational subzone of Nerodime on the 6th of July, 1998 --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that you were appointed -- you yourself were appointed to the subzone of Nerodimlje at this time; I understand that. What I'm asking is: In the interview, the OTP interview, you say that this structure that you have drawn is effective, that is it's in place at the time of the first offensive. And that's how it was, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time of the offensive in July, the structure was built up on the basis of subzones. There existed the operational subzone of Pastrik and of Nerodime. The Pastrik subzone was on one side of Berisa and the Nerodime on the other. This is how the guerrilla units functioned during the first offensive. In the part where I was appointed commander of subzone, I did my best to coordinate the units and their actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And in the Pastrik subzone at the time of the first offensive, the structure looked like this: There was Klecka and these units in these various villages. Isn't that right, the structure that you've drawn?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time of the offensive, Klecka was in the Pastrik operational subzone, as was Luznica which belonged to Suhareke municipality. And since it was determined on the basis of municipalities, Drenica was in the municipality of Gllogoc and it belonged to the subzone of Drenica. According to General Staff, the subzones were organised as per municipalities and the units were to act according to the municipalities that they belonged. This was a sort of -- it can be described as three subzones. A restructuring began and the 121st Brigade was formed in the beginning of August. This structure, as I said, existed for a short period of time when the guerrilla units coordinated -- were coordinated or led by the General Staff spokesperson.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But my question is: This diagram that you drew, and if you could look at the diagram, this diagram. In the interview you said that at the time of the first offensive, this structure that you drew was effective, that it existed.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These units existed and were operational, but the link with the General Staff was through the subzone commanders. I was the commander of the Nerodime subzone and coordinated for the units that were operational, as was the unit for Zborce, Pjetershtice. And these were the activities that I coordinated with Klecka with General Staff or Jakup Krasniqi, who was for a certain period of time in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But if that's the case, then why did you say -- can you explain why you said, please, in the interview that at the time of the first offensive, this structure that you've drawn was in place? Can you explain that, why you said that, if that's not the truth?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I described the structure and I said that these points functioned and I described it as a structure that could have functioned in one period of time of one offensive that occurred sometime in mid-July. This structure could have functioned in relation of General Staff, but there was also a structure that was being formed, the structure of subzones, and the subzone commanders were being appointed. This was in the -- early July when we were facing the offensive and were not able to continue with the building of the commanding structure. This was a period where we were not able to coordinate the activities and create a subzone structure but the coordination was done with -- between the units and the General Staff through Jakup Krasniqi whose role was dual and very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So, Mr. Buja, just picking up on the first part of your answer here, are you saying that this structure that you drew could have functioned in mid-July, that this is --

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying that the form of subzone could have functioned. With my appointment as commander of subzone I did my best to coordinate the units. As for this structure, it could have functioned in a period that I cannot determine. Simply, it is a very brief period and I don't know if it is correct as a description because the guerrilla units were not coordinated from the subzone but they coordinated directly from Klecka and Jakup Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware that Jakup Krasniqi has testified in this trial?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And are you aware that he testified that that he did not have an operational role but he was part of the political wing of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I heard him and I know his role, the role of Jakup Krasniqi. I said earlier and even today I remember that Jakup Krasniqi was the only member of General Staff whom we knew because he came out publicly and we tried through him to coordinate our work. This doesn't mean that he dealt with the operations, but through him we communicated with other members of the General Staff and through him we received orders, instructions, and information regarding further activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But that's an operational role, isn't it? If he's communicating orders from the General Staff, then he's then in an operational role. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did not have an operational role. He informed us because, realistically, we did not know the structure of the General Staff and we didn't know who were its members. And through Jakup Krasniqi we were informed and even the appointment of the subzone commander of Nerodime was given to me through Jakup Krasniqi. As for the rest of the General Staff members, we were not familiar with them. At that time the General Staff was acting half illegally and the role of Jakup Krasniqi was the one of a mediator. Or -- I don't really know how to call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, can you explain why the General Staff would communicate orders through somebody whose function was in the political wing and who was spokesman rather than somebody who was on the operational side of the KLA? Why would the General Staff do that, do you know?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the reason was their illegality, to remain unknown for us. Because it was a great danger to know a member of the General Staff who dealt with operations because the aim of the occupying forces was to attack and to know the General Staff's commander at that time. The occupying forces would attack them, as was the case with Prekaz with the concentration of Serb forces in Prekaz when the attack on the legendary commander Adem Jashari was launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja -- Mr. Buja, isn't it the fact that the orders were not communicated through Jakup Krasniqi but they were communicated through Fatmir Limaj, and that's why you thought that he was a member of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Fatmir Limaj did not communicate the orders. The orders, the instructions, they came from Jakup Krasniqi. If Jakup Krasniqi was asked about this issue, he would have given explanation. If we were given an order or instruction from the General Staff, that would be conveyed to us through Jakup Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to turn to a different subject. You have told us that there was --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But before I do, I would ask, Your Honour, that this diagram U003-3675 be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P159.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, you have talked about fighting that occurred in Carraleve in June of 1998. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was fighting in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And were you present for that fighting?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I went to this fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you engaged in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to these fightings and I was involved in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you fighting in Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember the date that you were fighting?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the dates, it's really difficult for me to remember them but of course it was June, mid-June. I fought in July as well, especially with the Zborce unit which was in a very bad position in July when it was forced to withdraw. And for Carraleve-Belince line, I happened to go there in June and July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In -- the fighting in Zborce in July when the unit was forced to withdraw, was that during -- was that at the end of July?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was -- the fighting occurred on the 25th or the 26th of July in this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you give the order to the unit to withdraw?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The withdrawal of this unit was carried out without an order. And due to the attack of the Serb forces, on this fighting Ruzhdi Salihu was killed and we had two or three injured soldiers, soldiers left with very few weapons and ammunition; they were forced to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you later have problems about this withdrawal? Did that cause you problems later on?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This withdrawal caused me problems, not only the problem of the withdrawal of Zborce unit which was positioned on the second front line as we called it. I carried out the withdrawal because on the fightings of 24th of July, if not mistaken, after this there was fighting in Fushtice and there the Fustica unit withdrew as well after an hour or an hour and a half of combat. My going there and my meeting with Isak Musliu, we started an operation to make these positions -- to take possession of these positions again. There was fighting on the front line of Blinaje unit as well, a front line which was quite long and the number of soldiers was very small. On that night through Resinovc village I was forced to leave Fustica and go to Blinaje and there I tried to coordinate the activity of this unit which was at great risk. The following morning there was severe fighting in Zborce as well. My movement was mainly along Blinaje and Zborce, and on the 26th of July when the fighting spread on 26th of July, the Zborce unit withdrew to its second positions and the situation in which the units found themselves forced me to withdraw the units because Komorane and Pjetershtice area was at danger and I thought that the tendency of the Serb army was to join their forces, those in Komorane and in Zborce. This tendency of the Serb forces left an encirclement the Blinaje unit and also put at risk the Pjetershtice unit which was positioned in Carraleve gorge. I sent a soldier to request the withdrawal of Petrastica units in Carraleve where fighting was ongoing, and I faced some problems. The problem that I faced was of a strange nature because orders were not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. carried out, proposals were not heard, my proposals were not heard. This unit was mainly under the influence of Ramiz Qeriqi, as was the unit in Zborce. I during the 26th of July even after midnight I was with Blinaje unit and I was forced to withdraw this unit and to seek positioning of units in the defending of the gorge where the population, civilian population, was sheltering.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: After -- after that happened, after that withdrawal, what kind of problems can you -- can you describe for us what kind of problems you had with regard to that issue?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the withdrawal of these units, a propaganda was launched against my personality and it was described as my desertion, as a wrong move which damaged the KLA warfare, and it resembled a special war against me as a war personality. This caused many problems and myself on 27th or 28th of July, I was forced to answer this propaganda which was -- had its roots in the special warfare waged by the Serbs. I found the base of this propaganda the result of the old maxim divide and rule and this had an impact on my personality and even jeopardised me physically. That's why I withdrew to Javor village to consult Jakup Krasniqi about further actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how did you respond to these accusations? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally I was a person that did not -- did not refute these allegations directly because I understood the underlying motive of these allegations and the specific target aimed at me. That's why I went to Jakup Krasniqi, explained to him my situation, told him about the propaganda campaign being conducted and the fact that it was targeting me specifically. I told Jakup Krasniqi that I would no longer be performing my duties as subzone commander as a result of this propaganda. I demanded that measures be taken against my if I had acted erroneously or those that were spreading such misinformation should be held accountable. I asked him that for me to continue to be in the position of the commander of the Nerodime subzone, they had to specify my tasks as a commander as well as a commanding structure that I had to organise along with an area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And who was it that you expected to either take measures against you or hold accountable those who spread information?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I expected the General Staff of course as the highest body of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you say that you -- you said that measures should be taken against you if you -- it was found that you acted erroneously, what kind of measures were you talking about?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am talking about the measures that could be taken by the General Staff. I thought that I might be discharged from my duty or even be imprisoned if -- even though I didn't know that any superior had been imprisoned until then. But this is what I wanted the General Staff to do, that is to take some actions, some measures because of this, as I said, specific struggle aimed at me which had harmed me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did the General Staff do?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the moment they didn't do anything specific, but Jakup Krasniqi -- with whom my brother, Rame Buja stayed, he was his advisor at the time -- explained to me they would see the possibility of the re-organisation of the military structure and to try to clarify what I wanted from the General Staff and that they would consider a re-organisation of the military structure there. After some time, not a long time actually, I -- from -- during which I didn't carry out my function as Pastrik subzone -- zone -- subzone, we were discussing the suggestions given by the General Staff about the re-organisation, that is that the units that had created problems - Kroimire, Pjetershtice, Zborce, Blinaje, and Fushtice - should be attached to the Pastrik operational subzone and think of establishing a brigade in that area as a result of the very good territorial ties these units had. And then continue with the organisation of the units. After some time --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, is this at the end of July/beginning of August period?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the time period during which I went to Jakup Krasniqi to inform him of what was happening and to demand these measures from the General Staff was end of July, whereas the answer from the General Staff to go to Albania came to me on the 10th or 15th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you go to Albania?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went through Malisheve municipality, Suhareke, Prizren, and then I crossed over to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: During the time period of June and July of 1998 when there was fighting, for example you've given us the example of fighting at Carraleve, did units from other villages come to assist in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some units have come to assist us because usually the attack was done against -- one unit was organised against one unit and other units came to assist that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how did that happen? How did -- how did units get sent from one village to assist another unit in another village with fighting?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually the unit helped another unit. It was an easy thing to do because fire shots could be heard from Lapusnik to Carraleve or from Klecka to Blinaje. It was an area from where the sound of fighting could be heard and the unit went -- a unit went to the zone of fighting after hearing the fire shots. Sometimes we have sent a soldier to ask other units to help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was this assistance from one unit to another unit ever organised by Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that it was organised by Klecka. I do know, however, that I have organised the passage of one unit to Carraleve when there has been fighting there or a unit in Fushtice, Blinaje, just as I have taken part of the unit from Zborce to fight in Fushtice. There have been instances when from Lapusnik gorge units have come to our rescue in fighting, as the case was on the 24th of July in Fushtice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you say you can't say it was organised by Klecka, what do you mean when you say that, that you don't know or that it wasn't?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very well how one unit helped another, at least in the area of my responsibility when I was a commander. Initially I was a coordinator and later the commander of the subzone. I knew very well when this occurred in several instances. When it came to assist other units like Luzhnice, Lapusnik, that was a marginal assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But my question is: Did -- was this ever organised by Klecka, this assistance? Did Klecka ever play a role in -- in having a unit come to the assistance of another unit?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The form of organisation of assistance from one unit to another was not organised by Klecke, but the Klecke unit of course assisted other units. Part of the unit came from Klecke to assist us in fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But your testimony is that other than occasions when the Klecka unit itself went to assist other units, then Klecka did not play a role in sending one unit to help another unit. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less this is how it was. I don't know that there was any form of coordination of the units by Klecka, with the exception of some instance when we have been unable to communicate with other units and through radio use that could -- that there was in Klecke, they could call some units to come for assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When that happened, would you radio to Klecka and then Klecka would radio to the other units?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period up to when I went to Albania, I didn't have radio communication, radio use, so I wasn't able to communicate by radio. But in Klecka there was radio communication and if they heard that there was fighting, of course Klecka must have invited the units to help.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did that happen? Do you know that that happened?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if that has happened, but I do know that the units of -- the unit of Lapusnik headed by Voglushi and the unit of Luznica commanded by Kumanova have come to my rescue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn now to resume tomorrow at 2.15 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I was off the air. We'll adjourn now and resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if I could raise one matter before we rise very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I anticipate that we might reach some cross-examination tomorrow. That being so, certainly it would be of assistance to us if it would be possible for us to have the reasons for the decision, because clearly it may reflect on the current testimony. I hope that's not too difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It creates a problem because of other commitments on our time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If it's possible, it will be done but I would not think it likely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
